graph.summary: Isoniazid → Enoyl-[acyl-carrier-protein] reductase [NADH] InhA → mycolic acid biosynthetic process → Mycobacterium tuberculosis → Pulmonary Tuberculosis

evidence.snippet: Isoniazid (INH), a treatment for tuberculosis (TB), targets the enzyme InhA (mycobacterium enoyl acyl carrier protein reductase)
evidence.explanation: Isoniazid targets and inhibits InhA, the enoyl-ACP reductase of M. tuberculosis, reducing its catalytic activity.

paper.title: Unlocking InhA: Novel approaches to inhibit Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

evidence.snippet: InhA is the primary target of isoniazid (INH), one of the most effective compounds to treat TB.
evidence.explanation: InhA is directly identified as the primary enzymatic target of isoniazid in M. tuberculosis.

paper.title: Discovery of new diaryl ether inhibitors against Mycobacterium tuberculosis targeting the minor portal of InhA.

evidence.snippet: InhA, is a member of an unusual FAS-II system that prefers longer chain fatty acyl substrates for the purpose of synthesizing mycolic acids, a major component of mycobacterial cell walls.
evidence.explanation: InhA (enoyl-ACP reductase) is part of the FAS-II system responsible for mycolic acid biosynthesis, confirming it positively regulates this process.

paper.title: Crystal structure of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis enoyl-ACP reductase, InhA, in complex with NAD+ and a C16 fatty acyl substrate.

evidence.snippet: Upon activation, INH inhibits InhA, thereby disrupting mycolic acid biosynthesis, a crucial process for maintaining Mtb's distinctive, lipid-rich cell wall.
evidence.explanation: Mycolic acid biosynthesis is explicitly described as a process occurring in and essential for M. tuberculosis (Mtb).

paper.title: Uncovering the structural impact of KatG Ser315 mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis via cryo-EM.
paper.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

evidence.snippet: Enzymes belonging to the type II fatty acid synthase system (FAS-II) are involved in the biosynthesis of mycolic acids, cell envelope components essential for mycobacterial survival.
evidence.explanation: Mycolic acid biosynthesis by the FAS-II system occurs in mycobacteria; loss of this process is lethal to the organism.

paper.title: Discovery of new diaryl ether inhibitors against Mycobacterium tuberculosis targeting the minor portal of InhA.

evidence.snippet: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the causative agent of tuberculosis (TB), is responsible for a global health burden affecting over a quarter of the world's population.
evidence.explanation: M. tuberculosis is the established causative agent of tuberculosis, including pulmonary tuberculosis.

paper.title: Uncovering the structural impact of KatG Ser315 mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis via cryo-EM.
paper.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
